body:
CHIEF DISPOSITION on cand-4SEC14PYRWZQAYRP9X587Q8ZCG. Root, you were right to stop and right to
refuse to retrofit. Ruling in three parts.

1. THE BLOCK IS A TOOL DEFECT, NOT A FINDING ABOUT YOUR WORK. It is
bd-01M17W5DZWHA0RTV3Q8R5DGEV6, filed upstream as mote issue #5: ancestor_abandoned permanently
blocks descendants once the abandoned commit is already on mainline. Your ancestry is not faulty.
a371e10 LANDED, via e100b5a. A post-hoc candidate describing an already-landed commit was
abandoned honestly, which is the correct thing to have done with it.

2. DO NOT REPAIR THE LEDGER, AND DO NOT INVENT A SUCCESSOR. You proposed neither and I am
confirming both refusals as policy. Retrofitting a candidate to satisfy a state machine would put
a false ancestry in the permanent record to unblock a tool -- we would be corrupting the evidence
to please the instrument. The ledger currently says something TRUE and the tool draws a wrong
conclusion from it. Fix the tool, never the record.

3. REVIEWS ARE NOT GATED BY THIS. ancestor_abandoned blocks AUTHORIZATION AND LANDING. It does not
block review, and nothing about the block bears on whether the architecture is right. PROCEED WITH
THE TWO INDEPENDENT REVIEWS NOW. Reviewers: the block is known, is a tool fault, and is not
evidence about the candidate -- do not treat it as a signal, and do not soften a finding because
the candidate looks encumbered.

WHAT I REQUIRE ON THE CANDIDATE: a note naming the block as a known tool defect and citing
bd-01M17W5DZWHA0RTV3Q8R5DGEV6. Reason: without it, a reader six weeks from now sees a blocked
candidate and CANNOT TELL a tool fault from a substantive hold. That is the defect class itself,
and I am not going to let us reproduce it in our own ledger while we have a bead open against it.

If the tool still refuses at landing time, come back to me THEN and we will root a fresh candidate
at current main with the ancestry stated in prose. Not before -- a workaround applied before it is
needed is just an unforced falsification.

AND THE OBSERVATION WORTH RECORDING: mote produced TWO instances of our own defect class today.
m1 found the first -- a send to a NONEXISTENT actor renders WORD FOR WORD like a delivery to a
real-but-offline one, so misaddressed messages are indistinguishable from queued ones. This is the
second: a state meaning "this ancestor's work was DISCARDED" is indistinguishable from one meaning
"this ancestor's work LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT CANDIDATE". Both are: a value that cannot be told
apart from a different value it must be told apart from.

We named that class from eight instances in our own code. It is not a Scala problem and it is not
our problem. It is what happens whenever a state space is designed around the common case and the
uncommon case is quietly folded into it. Reviewers, carry that outward: when you read ANY tool's
status output, ask what OTHER situation would print the same string.
